purpose: Quantify how strongly the bounded core-Nipponocirsium orientation chronology overlaps Mid-Pleistocene timing so temporal coincidence is not misread as an independent trigger test.
chronology_enumeration: same deterministic 16 x 10 marginal-node grid used by the frozen orientation-origin analysis; retain parent > child with duration >= 0.010 Ma and add central 0.74/0.79 Ma pair
interpretation: Because nearly all admissible chronology pairs overlap a broad 0.7-0.9 Ma Mid-Pleistocene band, saying the orientation branch overlaps the Mid-Pleistocene Transition is largely a consequence of the chronology constraint itself. It may be reported as regional/global temporal context, but it cannot discriminate a trigger mechanism without an independently specified event-level exposure test.
claim_boundary: Temporal overlap is not a causal test.
The Mid-Pleistocene Transition is not inferred to have caused capitulum orientation change.
The chronology grid is a scenario envelope, not posterior event-time probability.
Regional sea-level/oceanographic changes around 0.8 Ma remain context until local paleogeography and repeated trait events are independently evaluated.
